BACKGROUND (measured live on staging, scene 1A, after the semantic reveal fallback shipped): the fallback (`_semantic_authored_handoff` in cloudflare.py calling `reaches_reveals` in jev_questions.py) matched 'Examine the papers in the KMS drawer.' and delivered the memory card. But 'Examine the papers and notes in my initials-marked drawer.' and 'Search my initials-marked drawer for hidden clues.' did NOT match, and the narrator then invented a clue ('a small piece of paper stuck between the stapler and the wall', 'Meet me at the old warehouse at midnight') that sent the player off the story. Cause 1: the Jev question carries only the command and the reveal's `earn_when` sentence ('searches the KMS drawer or the space beneath it'). The judge is not told that 'the drawer with her initials', 'initials-marked drawer' and 'the KMS drawer' are one thing. Cause 2: when the command reaches a place or thing that holds an unrevealed reveal but nothing matched, the narrator is free to make up a clue.

FIX 1 (names for the judge): extend `reaches_reveals(ask, command, candidates)` so each candidate may carry a list of names (candidate tuple of (id, sentence) stays accepted; also accept (id, sentence, names)). For each eligible candidate, build names from its `entity_ids`: each entity's display name and aliases and its placement text, taken from the loaded package world (find how cloudflare.py already resolves entity names, for example in `_placement_rules`, `_protagonist_name` or the world model helpers; reuse that and do not invent a new source). Cap at 12 names per candidate, drop names of the protagonist, and de-duplicate. Add to each question's instructions a plain sentence such as: 'These all mean the same thing as the words in the sentence: <names joined with ; >.' Also add the candidate statement as a second sentence of context. Keep the strict rule (the whole action, not part). Keep the 6-candidate cap, the fail-closed behaviour and every existing guard.

FIX 2 (no invented clue): in cloudflare.py, when the semantic fallback ran (or could have run) and returned no match, and the command mentions (whole word, case-insensitive, possessive tolerant) any name or alias of any entity of an eligible-but-unmatched reveal candidate, add ONE narrator rule to the turn rules for that turn: 'The player found nothing new here.' then a second short rule 'Show only what the story already says about it.' Write it at an 8th grade reading level, two short sentences, one idea each, no jargon, and add it through the same helper that builds the turn rules so the normal turn path gets it (the opening path does not need it). Do not add it on authored handoff turns. Put the logic in one small helper.

Tests (tests/test_semantic_reveal_match.py, fakes only): the question text now includes the names and the statement; names are capped at 12 and de-duplicated and exclude the protagonist; a command that names an alias reaches the same candidate through a fake ask that answers yes only when the question text contains the alias; the no-clue rule appears when the command names an eligible entity and nothing matched; it does not appear when the command names nothing from an eligible candidate, when a handoff matched, or on a negated command. Run: TMPDIR=/tmp uv run pytest -q -x ; uv run ruff check --fix . ; uv run ruff format . . Write ./notes.md at the worktree root with what changed and the exact new wording.

An affordance that is absent from `shown` must be ignored, never counted as unshown. Items revealed only later in the scene (the `later` list) never make a transition silent. Keep the output shape.
